articles.title: 'Big Bang' Fix Puts Voyager Across the 'One Light-Day' Mark
articles.description: Flashback to 1977. Jimmy Carter was U.S. president, Star Wars was a box office hit, and the two Voyager spacecraft departed on an historic Grand Tour of the solar system. Now, teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are working to keep the missions active, as they push the boundaries of interstellar space beyond the solar system.
articles.summary: Voyager spacecraft, launched in 1977, have achieved the remarkable milestone of crossing the one light-day distance from Earth, continuing their unprecedented journey through interstellar space. This achievement represents humanity's most distant operational spacecraft exploration.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay occurring approximately once every 10 billion instances, marking a major breakthrough in particle physics. This discovery brings scientists closer to understanding the exotic particles of the zeptoverse.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists using the Large Hadron Collider have peered into the zeptoverse, a minuscule quantum realm where exotic particles may hide. This landmark research expands humanity's ability to probe the fundamental nature of reality.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers have observed two different kinds of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart—an unprecedented cosmic event. These extraordinarily energetic phenomena offer new insights into the most violent processes in the universe.

articles.title: The ELT Can Probe Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies and Their Dark Matter Mysteries
articles.description: Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies are strange because they're as large as the Milky Way, but have far fewer stars. It's as if they're puffed up for some reason. Determining what's going on with them could help confirm the Lambda-CDM model. A new proposed instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope could give astronomers their best look yet at these strange galaxies.
articles.summary: The Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) is opening new pathways to study ultra-diffuse galaxies, which are as large as the Milky Way yet contain far fewer stars, offering crucial insights into dark matter distribution. This capability promises to unlock mysteries about why these galaxies have such unusual structures.

articles.title: NASA's Twin Spacecraft Will Execute Powered Slingshot Maneuvers on Their Way to Mars
articles.description: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features a pair of identical spacecraft on their way to Mars. They launched outside of the normal launch window, so they'll perform powered slingshot maneuvers to boost their speed. Once there, they'll "fly" in formation and study how the solar wind interacts with what remains of Mars ancient magnetosphere.
articles.summary: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features twin spacecraft executing innovative powered slingshot maneuvers on their journey to Mars, launching outside typical mission windows. This mission advances our understanding of the Martian atmosphere and space weather interactions.

articles.title: A Mighty Wind Blew Away Gas and Made Early Galaxies Brighter
articles.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies about 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang. But these galaxies should have been far less common so soon after the Big Bang. Researchers may have figured this out: Powerful ultraviolet (Lyman-alpha) radiation produced by dense clusters of young stars acted like a leaf blower, driving light-blocking gas and dust out of the galaxy and thereby making the galaxies appear brighter.
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope observations of the early universe reveal that powerful stellar winds blew away gas and enhanced galaxy brightness in the cosmic dawn. This discovery provides new insights into how the first galaxies shaped the early universe.

articles.title: Want to fly to the moon? NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis program
articles.description: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis program.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA is recruiting new astronauts to support the Artemis program's ambitious goal of establishing a permanent lunar base and returning humans to the Moon. This initiative represents humanity's next giant leap in space exploration and lunar settlement.

articles.title: Untangling the patterns of the cosmic microwave background to better understand the early universe
articles.description: A figure in red trudges across a blanket of white. Snow squeaks under the scientist's feet, too dry to be slick or soft. Only a line of flags and a few large buildings—the scientist's destination—break up the landscape. The sun hovers on the horizon, never quite setting against a blue sky devoid of clouds.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists are using advanced analysis of cosmic microwave background patterns to unlock secrets of the early universe's composition and evolution. These detailed studies refine our understanding of the universe's first moments after the Big Bang.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Fresh volcanic activity detected on Mars suggests the Red Planet may still be geologically dynamic, challenging previous assumptions about its dormant state. This discovery opens new possibilities for understanding Mars's interior and past habitability.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
articles.description: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky. The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust. Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.
articles.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has discovered two previously unknown satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, with evidence suggesting hundreds more companions await discovery. This breakthrough expands our understanding of galactic structure and dark matter distribution.

articles.title: A dead star's mysterious rings reveal what could happen when our Sun dies
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star, revealing a possible preview of our Solar System's distant future. The two rings are separated by a mysterious gap that researchers believe is maintained by surviving planetary bodies, including one potentially as large as Pluto or the Moon. Their different chemical compositions suggest they may contain the remains of separate destroyed planets.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a remarkable double ring of planetary debris around a dead star, providing insight into what may eventually happen to our own solar system. This stellar relic offers a fascinating glimpse into distant planetary futures.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has obtained detailed images of the asteroid pair targeted by NASA's groundbreaking 2022 kinetic impact experiment. This follow-up mission validates humanity's first planetary defense test and advances asteroid science.

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.description: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.summary: Scientists are modeling atmospheres of lifeless planets to better distinguish between inhabited and barren worlds in the search for extraterrestrial life. This innovative approach enhances our ability to identify potentially habitable exoplanets.

articles.title: Une nouvelle mini-lune tourne autour de la Terre, et on a cru que c’était un morceau d’Apollo 13
articles.description: Le Minor Planet Center a confirmé le 29 octobre 2026 que la Terre héberge une nouvelle mini-lune, un caillou de 1 à 2 mètres baptisé 2026 QQ8. Des scientifiques l'ont même soupçonné d'être un débris spatial, allant jusqu'à parler d'un reste de la mission Apol…
articles.summary: Earth has acquired a new mini-moon, a 1-2 meter rock confirmed by the Minor Planet Center, initially thought to be debris from Apollo 13. This discovery expands our understanding of Earth's orbital companions.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional dim satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, including an ultra-faint dwarf. These findings enhance our mapping of the galactic neighborhood.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: New research uses nanohertz gravitational waves to constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn. This work reveals how black hole pairs behaved in the early universe.

articles.title: Le vol lunaire Artemis II a provoqué une déchirure atmosphérique inédite
articles.description: En traversant les couches supérieures du ciel pour son périple autour de la Lune, l'équipage d'Artemis II a involontairement laissé une signature saisissante au-dessus du continent américain, au point de perturber les signaux GPS.
articles.summary: The Artemis II lunar mission created an unprecedented atmospheric phenomenon as the spacecraft traversed the upper atmosphere during its lunar trajectory. This discovery reveals new insights about spacecraft-atmosphere interactions.

articles.title: Trump's makes nuclear push in space exploration, sets 2-yr deadline for Nasa's Mars mission
articles.description: NASA is gearing up to launch an innovative nuclear-powered spacecraft towards Mars within the next two years. This ambitious mission is set to pioneer advanced nuclear-electric propulsion technology, critical for future exploration efforts. With a focus on re…
articles.summary: NASA is developing an innovative nuclear-powered spacecraft for Mars missions with an ambitious two-year deployment timeline. This cutting-edge propulsion technology represents a major advancement in deep space exploration.

articles.title: SpaceX va tenter de rattraper Starship avec deux bras géants : une manœuvre aussi spectaculaire que risquée
articles.description: SpaceX vise le 13 novembre pour le quinzième vol d'essai intégré de Starship, au cours duquel l'entreprise tentera de rattraper à la fois le booster Super Heavy et l'étage supérieur à l'aide de la tour de lancement de Starbase. Si elle réussit, cette double c…
articles.summary: SpaceX plans to attempt its most spectacular maneuver yet during Starship's fifteenth integrated flight test on November 13, using two giant mechanical arms to catch the vehicle. This innovative landing technique represents a revolutionary approach to spacecraft recovery.

articles.title: Astronomy Picture of the Day - A Farewell to Swift
articles.description: Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia. The featured image is a mosaic…
articles.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory concludes nearly 22 years of groundbreaking service studying gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic phenomena. The mission's legacy represents a remarkable achievement in space-based astronomy.

articles.title: Studie: Artemis-II-Start verursacht Störung in der oberen Atmosphäre
articles.description: Die historische Artemis-II-Mission der NASA hat im April 2026 nicht nur Astronauten um den Mond fliegen lassen, sondern auch gewaltige Löcher in die obere Erdatmosphäre gerissen. Forscher warnen nun, dass solche Ereignisse GPS-Signale stören können.(Weiter le…
articles.summary: NASA's historic Artemis II mission in April 2026 flies astronauts around the Moon while providing unexpected scientific data about atmospheric effects. The mission demonstrates the complex interactions between spaceflight and Earth's upper atmosphere.

articles.title: Musk projects SpaceX annualized revenue could top $500 billion by end of 2027
articles.description:
SpaceX's AI-driven revenue ambitions could redefine its market valuation, shifting comparisons from aerospace to major tech companies.
The post Musk projects SpaceX annualized revenue could top $500 billion by end of 2027 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
articles.summary: SpaceX projects annualized revenue could exceed $500 billion by end of 2027 through AI-driven commercial initiatives. The ambitious growth forecast reflects the company's expanding role in commercial spaceflight and space infrastructure.

articles.title: Our Sun’s Undiscovered Stellar Nemesis Is Still Out There, Says Physicist
articles.description: The decades old idea that our solar system’s Oort Cloud is continually perturbed by a heretofore undetected low mass Red Dwarf star remains the best explanation for periodicities found in Earth’s impact record.  Or so says a well known physicist who has long championed this idea.
articles.summary: Physicists continue investigating the decades-old hypothesis of an undiscovered low-mass red dwarf star in the Oort Cloud that may perturb our solar system. This theoretical stellar companion could help explain anomalies in comet trajectories and outer solar system dynamics.

articles.title: Earth's Gravity May Have Kept the Early Moon's Volcanic Heart Beating
articles.description: We typically think of the Moon as a static, floating object that has remained the same for basically its entire lifetime, with an occasional asteroid impact serving as an exception. That understanding is grounded in physics - the Moon should have cooled rapidly after forming when a huge protoplanet hit the early Earth around 4.5 billion years ago. But, some lunar material returned from the Chang’e-5 mission was notably formed only around two billion years ago, yet appeared to be volcanic in origin. So how did a world that was supposed to have settled down without volcanism remain hot enough to create these materials more than two billion years after its violent birth? A new paper from Miao Chen of the Chengdu University of Technology and his colleagues, and recently published in the journal Planet, offers an explanation - tidal heating.
articles.summary: New research reveals that Earth's gravity may have sustained the Moon's volcanic activity in its early history, challenging the conventional view of the Moon as a static celestial body. This discovery reshapes our understanding of lunar evolution and tidal interactions.

articles.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
articles.description: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). A new paper from a team of researchers led by Dr. Silvia Protopapa of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Southwest Research Institute, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, details JWST’s findings on the water ice content of this most recent visitor from beyond our solar system.
articles.summary: Analysis of interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS demonstrates that water ice behaves consistently across different star systems, suggesting universal physical laws govern composition in alien systems. This finding strengthens our understanding of chemistry throughout the cosmos.

articles.title: Game theory helps SETI search for alien civilizations
articles.description: The search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) is mostly concerned with where to look for technosignatures from another civilization. Between 2012 and 2015, SETI's Project Phoenix targeted about 1,000 sun-like stars for signs of intelligent life. But where to look might not be as important as when to look, according to scientists at SETI.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Game theory approaches are enhancing SETI's search strategies for detecting technosignatures from extraterrestrial civilizations. This innovative methodology optimizes where and how we search for signs of alien intelligence.

articles.title: 'Stupendously large' primordial black holes ruled out as a dark matter source
articles.description: Primordial black holes are hypothetical objects that could have formed directly from dense clumps of matter in the very early universe. If they exist, their dramatic origins would set them apart from the black holes we see today, which form when massive stars collapse. Some theories suggest that "stupendously large" primordial black holes could account for a significant share of the universe's elusive dark matter.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Research ruled out stupendously large primordial black holes as a primary dark matter source through rigorous cosmological testing. This finding narrows the field of candidates and advances our understanding of dark matter's true nature.

articles.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
articles.description: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An alternative cosmological model proposing a 26.7 billion-year-old universe without dark matter or dark energy has successfully passed key observational tests. This theory offers an intriguing alternative framework for understanding cosmic structure and expansion.

articles.title: Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station
articles.description: A Pakistani astronaut will join the crew of China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft on a mission that would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing's space station, state media reported Saturday.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A Pakistani astronaut is set to board Shenzhou 24, becoming the first foreigner to visit China's space station. This historic mission represents growing international cooperation in human spaceflight and orbital research.
